hardware.cpu: Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-3612QM CPU @ 2.10GHz (Ivy Bridge, 2012-era laptop CPU)
hardware.gpu: none used — CPU-only inference, per this cycle's explicit requirement

methodology: Real, live calls against Ollama's HTTP API (http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate) for every installed candidate model, using the SAME real production task (add viewport-fit=cover to apps/survival/index.html's viewport meta tag) and the SAME prompt template lib/ollama-patch-adapter.js's buildPatchPrompt() uses in production. Not a synthetic/trivial probe — this measures the actual structured-patch-generation capability the production adapter depends on. num_ctx=8192 for all calls.
note: The first attempt at this benchmark used a 60s timeout and every single model timed out with zero exceptions — that number was corrected after a direct diagnostic call showed even the smallest model needs ~100s+ for a real ~5.3KB file (prompt EVALUATION, not generation, dominates cost on this CPU: 2095 prompt tokens took over 100s). Results below use the corrected, evidence-based timeout.

results.verdict: REJECTED — completed and returned schema-valid JSON, but the 'find' field was a literal echo of the prompt's placeholder text ('<exact substring>'), not real content copied from the file. Too small/weak to reliably follow the find/replace instruction on this task.

REJECTED — this was the pre-cycle default (chosen for trivial-prompt speed in an earlier cycle), but it is measurably too slow for a real file-editing prompt on this hardware. Never completed within 220s.

PASS but slow — correct output, but 203s is close to the timeout boundary and much slower than qwen3:1.7b despite being a similar-sized model. Its 'thinking'/reasoning mode (noted in an earlier cycle) likely adds real overhead here.
SELECTED — fastest AND correct: valid schema, and the 'find' text matched the real file content exactly once. Beat every other model on both speed and correctness, including larger ones.
REJECTED — the largest installed model, and the slowest: timed out just like qwen2.5:3b-instruct. Confirms bigger is not better on this CPU-only hardware for this task.

decision.reasoning: The smallest model that actually works well won, not the biggest — matching this cycle's explicit instruction to pick the minimal model that genuinely improves the result rather than escalating size by default. No new model was downloaded; all 5 candidates were already installed.
decision.timeoutReasoning: ~2.6x margin above the winning model's real 56.7s observed duration, to absorb normal variance and the MAX_PROMPT_CONTENT_BYTES budget (6000 bytes) being larger than the single file tested here.
